questions.text: बीजाण्ड का कौन-सा भाग कठोर होकर बीजावरण में परिवर्तित हो जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which part of the ovule hardens to form seed coat of a seed ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Integuments. The integuments are the outer protective layers of the ovule that harden and differentiate after fertilisation to form the tough seed coat (testa and tegmen). The funicle is the stalk, chalaza is the base, and nucellus is the nutritive tissue — none of these form the seed coat.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) अध्यावरण (इंटेगुमेंट) है। बीजाण्ड के अध्यावरण निषेचन के बाद कठोर होकर बीजावरण (टेस्टा और टेगमेन) का निर्माण करते हैं। बीजाण्ड-वृन्त, स्निभाग और बीजाण्डकाय बीजावरण नहीं बनाते।

questions.text:
ड्रग तथा ऐल्कोहॉल के विषय में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं:
(i) किशोर मित्रों के दबाव (प्रभाव) में अधिक शीघ्र आ जाते हैं।
(ii) ड्रग की लत के परिणामस्वरूप हमारे शरीर में उपस्थित संवेदीग्राहियों के प्रति सहनशीलता अधिक हो जाती है।
(iii) ऐल्कोहॉल केन्द्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है।
(iv) ड्रग के अत्यधिक उपयोग से ऊर्जा शक्ति बढ़ाने में सहायता मिलती है।
(v) उपचयी स्टेरॉइड्स आक्रामकता का अवनमन (कम) करते हैं।
सही कथन/कथनों वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Some statements regarding drugs and alcohol are given below:
(i) Adolescents are more vulnerable to peer pressure.
(ii) Drug addiction leads to increased tolerance level of the receptors present in our body.
(iii) Alcohol affects the central nervous system.
(iv) Excessive use of drugs helps to increase energy.
(v) Anabolic steroids decrease aggressiveness.
Choose the option with correct statement(s).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Statement (i) is correct — adolescents are indeed more susceptible to peer pressure. Statement (ii) is correct — drug addiction leads to increased tolerance of receptors, meaning more drug is needed for the same effect. Statement (iii) is correct — alcohol is a CNS depressant. Statement (iv) is incorrect because excessive drug use does not increase energy; it leads to dependence and deterioration. Statement (v) is incorrect because anabolic steroids actually increase aggressiveness, not decrease it.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। कथन (i), (ii) और (iii) सही हैं। ड्रग की लत से ग्राहियों में सहनशीलता बढ़ती है, ऐल्कोहॉल CNS को प्रभावित करता है, और किशोर पीयर प्रेशर में जल्दी आते हैं। कथन (iv) और (v) गलत हैं।

questions.text: प्रतिजैविक-प्रतिरोधी जीवाणु का प्रादुर्भाव जिस प्रकार के विकास का उदाहरण है, वह है:
questions.text_english: Appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of evolution due to:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Anthropogenic action. The development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is driven by human activities — specifically, the widespread and often indiscriminate use of antibiotics. This creates a selection pressure that favours resistant strains, making it a classic example of human-induced (anthropogenic) evolution. It is not adaptive radiation, divergent evolution, or artificial selection in the traditional sense.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) मानवजनित कार्यकलाप है। प्रतिजैविक दवाओं के अत्यधिक उपयोग से जीवाणुओं में प्रतिरोध विकसित होना मानव-प्रेरित विकास का उदाहरण है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
कथन I : टीकाकरण तथा प्रतिरक्षण कार्यक्रम का उपयोग करके हम चेचक (स्मॉलपॉक्स) का समूल उन्मूलन करने में समर्थ (सफल) हुए हैं।
कथन II : डिप्थीरिया तथा पोलियो के लिए टीके उपलब्ध हैं।
questions.text_english:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:
Statement I: Using vaccination and immunization programmes, we have been able to eradicate smallpox.
Statement II: Vaccines are available for diphtheria and polio.

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।

options_english.A: Both Statements I and II are false.
options_english.B: Both Statements I and II are true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both statements are true. Smallpox was officially declared eradicated in 1980 by the WHO, achieved through a global vaccination and immunization programme — making Statement I correct. Effective vaccines are indeed available for both diphtheria (part of DPT vaccine) and polio (OPV/IPV), making Statement II also correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं। चेचक का 1980 में WHO द्वारा उन्मूलन घोषित किया गया और डिप्थीरिया व पोलियो के लिए टीके उपलब्ध हैं।

questions.text: टेलर तथा उनके सहयोगियों ने क्रोमोसोमों (गुणसूत्रों) में डीएनए के अर्धसंरक्षी प्रतिकृतिकरण के गुण की पुष्टि हेतु अपना प्रयोग निम्नलिखित में से किस जीव पर किया ?
questions.text_english: Taylor and colleagues performed an experiment on which of the following organisms to provide proof for semi-conservative replication of DNA in chromosomes ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Vicia faba (broad bean). Taylor, Woods and Hughes (1957) used Vicia faba root tip cells along with radioactive thymidine (tritium-labelled) and autoradiography to demonstrate semi-conservative replication of DNA in eukaryotic chromosomes. Meselson and Stahl proved semi-conservative replication in E. coli, not Taylor.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) विशिया फाबा है। टेलर और उनके सहयोगियों ने विशिया फाबा की जड़ की नोक की कोशिकाओं पर प्रयोग करके गुणसूत्रों में अर्धसंरक्षी प्रतिकृतिकरण को सिद्ध किया।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा पारिस्थितिक तंत्र की प्रकार्यात्मक इकाई नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a functional unit of an ecosystem ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Stratification. The four functional components/processes of an ecosystem are productivity, decomposition, energy flow, and nutrient cycling. Stratification refers to the vertical layering of vegetation in a community and is a structural feature of an ecosystem, not a functional unit. Hence it is the odd one out.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) स्तरण है। पारितंत्र की चार प्रकार्यात्मक इकाइयाँ हैं — उत्पादकता, अपघटन, ऊर्जा प्रवाह और पोषक चक्रण। स्तरण एक संरचनात्मक लक्षण है, प्रकार्यात्मक इकाई नहीं।

questions.text: गोल्डन राइस एक उदीयमान पारजीनी फसल है। इसे जब खेतों में उगाने के लिए निर्मुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह सहायक होगी :
questions.text_english: Golden rice is a promising transgenic crop. When released for cultivation, it will help in :

options.A: पेट्रोल के समान इंधन के उत्पादन में
options.B: मानव में विटामिन A की कमी को कम करने में

options_english.B: Reduction of Vitamin A deficiency in humans

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Reduction of Vitamin A deficiency in humans. Golden rice is a genetically engineered variety of rice that has been modified to produce beta-carotene (a precursor of Vitamin A) in the endosperm. It was developed to address widespread Vitamin A deficiency, particularly in developing countries. It does not produce fuel, confer pest resistance, or herbicide tolerance.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। गोल्डन राइस में बीटा-कैरोटीन (विटामिन A का पूर्वगामी) उत्पन्न करने की क्षमता होती है, जो मानव में विटामिन A की कमी को दूर करने में सहायक है।

questions.text: मानव शरीर में प्रतिपिंड (एंटीबॉडी) निर्मित करने के लिए कौन-सी कोशिकाएँ उत्तरदायी हैं ?
questions.text_english: Which cells are responsible for producing antibodies in a human body ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) B-Lymphocytes. B-lymphocytes, when activated by an antigen, differentiate into plasma cells that secrete specific antibodies. Macrophages are phagocytic cells involved in antigen presentation. Helper T-cells coordinate the immune response but do not produce antibodies. Cytotoxic T-cells kill infected cells directly rather than producing antibodies.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) बी-लसीकाणु है। बी-लिम्फोसाइट सक्रिय होकर प्लाज्मा कोशिकाओं में बदल जाते हैं जो प्रतिपिंड का स्राव करती हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा जन्तु द्वितीयक उपभोक्ता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is a secondary consumer ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Fish. In a typical aquatic food chain: phytoplankton (producer) → zooplankton (primary consumer) → fish (secondary consumer) → hawk (tertiary consumer). A grasshopper and cow are primary consumers as they feed on plants. A hawk is typically a tertiary consumer. Fish, feeding on small invertebrates (primary consumers), acts as a secondary consumer.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) मछली है। मछली प्राथमिक उपभोक्ताओं (जैसे जलीय कीट) को खाती है, इसलिए यह द्वितीयक उपभोक्ता है। टिड्डा और गाय प्राथमिक, बाज तृतीयक उपभोक्ता है।

questions.text:
कॉलम I में दी गई मदों का कॉलम II में दी गई मदों से मिलान कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
कॉलम I : a. प्रारंभक (प्राइमर), b. निवेशी निष्क्रियता (इनसर्शनल इनऐक्टीवेशन), c. बायोरिएक्टर, d. अनुप्रवाह संसाधन
कॉलम II : i. β-गैलेक्टोसाइडेज़, ii. उत्पादों का पृथक्करण तथा परिष्करण (शोधन), iii. रासायनिक रूप से संश्लेषित ऑलिगोन्यूक्लियोटाइड्स, iv. सूक्ष्मजीवीय प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा विशिष्ट उत्पादों का वृहद् स्तर पर उत्पादन
questions.text_english:
Match Column I with Column II and select the correct option:
Column I: a. Primers, b. Insertional inactivation, c. Bioreactor, d. Downstream processing
Column II: i. β-galactosidase, ii. To separate and purify products, iii. Chemically synthesized oligonucleotides, iv. Large scale production of specific product of activity of microbes
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Primers are chemically synthesized short oligonucleotides (iii). Insertional inactivation uses the lacZ gene that codes for β-galactosidase (i) — when a foreign gene is inserted into the lacZ gene, enzyme activity is lost, allowing selection of recombinants. Bioreactors are used for large-scale production of desired products through microbial activity (iv). Downstream processing refers to separation and purification of the final product (ii).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। प्राइमर — ऑलिगोन्यूक्लियोटाइड (iii); निवेशी निष्क्रियता — β-गैलेक्टोसाइडेज (i); बायोरिएक्टर — वृहद् उत्पादन (iv); अनुप्रवाह संसाधन — पृथक्करण व शोधन (ii)।

questions.text:
उस कथन को पहचानिए जो डार्विन के विकासवाद का सही ढंग से वर्णन करता है।
(i) जीवों का अतिशय उत्पादन स्पर्धा उत्पन्न करता है।
(ii) विविधता आनुवंशिक (वंशागत) है जो विकास का कारक है।
(iii) उपार्जित लक्षण वंशानुगत होते हैं।
(iv) उत्तरजीविता अनुकूलित विशेषकों (लक्षणों) पर निर्भर करती है।
(v) अनुकूली विविधताओं के संग्रहित होने से नई जाति (स्पीशीज़) का उद्भव होता है।
सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
Identify the statements that correctly describe Darwin's Theory of Evolution.
(i) Overproduction of organisms leads to competition.
(ii) Variation is inherited and causes evolution.
(iii) Acquired characters are inherited.
(iv) Survival depends on favourable traits.
(v) New species arise due to accumulation of favourable variations.
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Darwin's theory includes: overproduction leads to a struggle for existence (i), heritable variation drives natural selection (ii), survival of the fittest — favourably adapted individuals survive (iv), and accumulation of favourable variations over generations leads to new species (v). Statement (iii) — inheritance of acquired characters — is Lamarck's concept, not Darwin's. Darwin did not propose that characters acquired during an organism's lifetime are inherited.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। कथन (i), (ii), (iv) और (v) डार्विन के विकासवाद के सही वर्णन हैं। कथन (iii) लैमार्क का सिद्धांत है, डार्विन का नहीं।

questions.text: हॉर्मोन-आधारित गर्भनिरोधक विधि (युक्ति) जो अंडोत्सर्जन को संदमित (अवरोधित) करता है :
questions.text_english: The method of contraception that is hormone-based and prevents ovulation is :

options.A: मुँह द्वारा खाई जाने वाली गोलियाँ (पिल्स)

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Oral Pills. Oral contraceptive pills contain synthetic progesterone and/or oestrogen which inhibit the secretion of LH and FSH from the pituitary, thereby preventing ovulation. Copper-T and Lippes loop are intrauterine devices that do not prevent ovulation but prevent implantation or fertilisation. Condoms are barrier methods with no hormonal action.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) मुँह से ली जाने वाली गोलियाँ हैं। इनमें सिंथेटिक हॉर्मोन होते हैं जो LH और FSH के स्राव को रोककर अंडोत्सर्जन को संदमित करते हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र को उनके लिए आवश्यक अणुओं के संश्लेषण हेतु ऊर्जा की सतत आवश्यकता होती है।
कारण (R) : यह ऊष्मागतिकी के दूसरे नियम के वैश्विक अव्यवस्था के बढ़ने की प्रवृत्ति को प्रभावहीन करने के लिए होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Ecosystems require a constant supply of energy to synthesize the molecules they require.
Reason (R): This is to counteract the universal tendency towards increasing disorderliness as per Second Law of Thermodynamics.
questions.instruction_line: सही उत्तर चुनिए: (A) दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है। (B) दोनों सही हैं लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) A सही है, R गलत है। (D) A गलत है, R सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose: (A) Both A and R true, R is correct explanation. (B) Both true, R not correct explanation. (C) A true, R false. (D) A false, R true.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. According to the Second Law of Thermodynamics, all systems tend towards increasing entropy (disorder). Living systems, including ecosystems, are highly ordered structures. To maintain this order and synthesize complex molecules, a continuous input of energy is required to counteract this natural tendency towards disorder — making Reason the correct explanation of the Assertion.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। ऊष्मागतिकी के दूसरे नियम के अनुसार प्रणालियाँ अव्यवस्था की ओर बढ़ती हैं; पारितंत्र को इसका प्रतिरोध करने हेतु सतत ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जीवाणु कोशिका की कोशिका झिल्ली को डीएनए पार नहीं कर सकता।
कारण (R) : डीएनए एक जलरागी अणु है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): DNA cannot pass through cell membrane of a bacterial cell.
Reason (R): DNA is a hydrophilic molecule.
questions.instruction_line: सही उत्तर चुनिए: (A) दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है। (B) दोनों सही हैं लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) A सही है, R गलत है। (D) A गलत है, R सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose: (A) Both A and R true, R is correct explanation. (B) Both true, R not correct explanation. (C) A true, R false. (D) A false, R true.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. DNA is indeed a hydrophilic (water-loving) molecule due to its negatively charged phosphate backbone. The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that is hydrophobic in its interior. Therefore, hydrophilic DNA cannot spontaneously pass through the lipid bilayer, which is why special methods such as using calcium chloride to create competent cells are needed for transformation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं। DNA जलरागी है इसलिए वह कोशिका झिल्ली (जो जल-विरागी है) को स्वतः पार नहीं कर सकता। इसीलिए जीवाणुओं को कैल्शियम क्लोराइड से संसाधित करके सक्षम कोशिकाएँ बनाई जाती हैं।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : सक्रिय आपंक में जीवाणुओं की बड़ी समष्टियाँ होती हैं।
कारण (R) : ये जीवाणु बायोगैस संयंत्र में मानव अपशिष्टों के अवायवीय पाचन में सहायता करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Activated sludge contains large population of bacteria.
Reason (R): These bacteria help in anaerobic digestion of human waste in biogas plant.
questions.instruction_line: सही उत्तर चुनिए: (A) दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है। (B) दोनों सही हैं लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) A सही है, R गलत है। (D) A गलत है, R सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose: (A) Both A and R true, R is correct explanation. (B) Both true, R not correct explanation. (C) A true, R false. (D) A false, R true.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both the Assertion and the Reason are individually true, but the Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion. Activated sludge does contain large populations of bacteria (Assertion is true). It is also true that some bacteria help in anaerobic digestion in biogas plants (Reason is true). However, activated sludge is used in secondary treatment of sewage (aerobic process), not in biogas plants. The bacteria in activated sludge function aerobically to decompose organic matter in sewage — this is unrelated to biogas plants. Hence the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

This allows precise size-based separation of DNA fragments.

questions.text_english:

key_points: Morgan crossed white-eyed, yellow-bodied female Drosophila with red-eyed, grey-bodied male; then test-crossed F1 females
Expected 1:1:1:1 ratio in testcross but got mostly parental types and very few recombinants — deviation from Mendel's law of independent assortment
Two terms: (1) Linkage — tendency of genes on the same chromosome to be inherited together; (2) Recombination — production of new gene combinations due to crossing over

questions.solution: Morgan performed dihybrid crosses in Drosophila melanogaster involving eye colour (red/white) and body colour (grey/yellow). He crossed white-eyed yellow-bodied females with red-eyed grey-bodied males. The F1 females (dihybrid) were then test-crossed. According to Mendel's law of independent assortment, a 1:1:1:1 ratio was expected. However, the results showed predominantly parental combinations (white-eyed yellow-body and red-eyed grey-body) and very few recombinant types. This was a significant deviation from Mendelian inheritance because the two genes were located on the same chromosome (sex chromosome) and tended to be inherited together, violating independent assortment. Morgan used the term linkage to describe the tendency of genes located on the same chromosome to stay together during inheritance. He used the term recombination to explain the small percentage of new combinations that arise due to crossing over (exchange of chromosome segments) during meiosis.

questions.text_english:
In vitro fertilization (IVF) is a popular method these days that is helping childless couples to bear a child.
(a) Write the different steps that are carried out in this technique.
(b) Would you consider gamete intra fallopian transfer as a type of IVF? Justify your answer.

key_points: Steps of IVF: ovarian stimulation, egg retrieval, sperm collection, fertilisation in lab, embryo culture, embryo transfer into uterus
GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) is not exactly IVF — it transfers gametes (not embryo) into the fallopian tube where natural fertilisation occurs inside the body
IVF involves fertilisation outside the body; GIFT involves fertilisation inside the fallopian tube, so it is a related ART but not a type of IVF

questions.solution:
The steps of IVF are: (1) The woman is given hormone injections to stimulate superovulation (production of multiple eggs). (2) Ova are retrieved from the ovary under ultrasound guidance. (3) Semen is collected from the male partner and sperm are capacitated. (4) Fertilisation is carried out in a culture medium in the laboratory — forming a zygote (test-tube fertilisation). (5) The fertilised egg is cultured until the 8-celled embryo stage. (6) The embryo is transferred into the uterus of the woman (Embryo Transfer / ET) for further development.

Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) should not be considered a type of IVF. In IVF, fertilisation occurs outside the body in laboratory conditions. In GIFT, the collected gametes (both ova and sperm) are transferred directly into the fallopian tube of the woman, where fertilisation occurs naturally inside the body. Since GIFT does not involve in vitro (outside the body) fertilisation, it is a different type of Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART), not IVF.

(b) Mention one advantage of apomictic seeds for farmers.

key_points: Apomixis can occur via: (1) diploid egg cell developing without fertilisation, (2) cells of nucellus proliferating and developing into embryos (adventive embryony)
Advantage: Hybrid seed production cost is greatly reduced as seeds maintain hybrid characters over generations without crossing every year

questions.solution:
Apomixis is the development of seeds without fertilisation. It can occur in the following ways: (1) In some species, a diploid egg cell (formed without meiosis, or by restoration of diploidy) develops directly into an embryo without fertilisation — this is called diplospory or apospory depending on the origin of the unreduced egg. (2) In adventive embryony, cells of the nucellus or integuments (somatic cells of the ovule) proliferate and develop into embryos directly, as seen in Citrus. These somatic embryos are genetically identical to the mother plant.

One major advantage for farmers is that hybrid seeds produced through apomixis retain their hybrid vigour (heterosis) over successive generations. This means farmers do not need to purchase new hybrid seeds every year — they can save seeds from their own crop, significantly reducing cultivation costs.

questions.text_english:
(a) What is meant by translation in protein synthesis?
(b) Explain charging of tRNA (aminoacylation of tRNA) and mention its importance in the process of translation.

key_points: Translation: process of decoding mRNA sequence into amino acid sequence (protein synthesis) using ribosomes and tRNA
Charging of tRNA: attachment of specific amino acid to its cognate tRNA by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase enzyme using ATP energy
Importance: ensures correct amino acid is brought to the ribosome, maintaining fidelity of the genetic code

questions.solution:
Translation is the process by which the nucleotide sequence of mRNA is decoded to synthesise a specific polypeptide (protein). It occurs on ribosomes with the help of tRNA molecules that carry amino acids and recognise mRNA codons through their anticodons.

Charging of tRNA (aminoacylation) is the process by which a specific amino acid is covalently attached to its corresponding tRNA molecule. This reaction is catalysed by a specific enzyme called aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, which uses ATP energy. Each aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase is highly specific — it recognises only one type of amino acid and its corresponding tRNA. The resulting charged tRNA is called aminoacyl-tRNA.

The importance of charging is that it ensures the correct amino acid is brought to the ribosome-mRNA complex. Since the genetic code is read via codon-anticodon base pairing, charging guarantees that the amino acid delivered matches the instruction encoded in the mRNA, thereby maintaining the fidelity and accuracy of protein synthesis.

questions.text_english:
(a) Who discovered Penicillin and how? Explain.
(b) Why is this discovery considered accidental?
(c) In what way did it prove to be a 'milestone' in the field of medicine?

key_points: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin in 1928 when he noticed a mould (Penicillium notatum) had contaminated his bacterial culture plate and created a clear zone of inhibition
It was accidental because Fleming had left the plate unattended and the contamination was unintentional
It was a milestone because Penicillin was the first antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections, saving millions of lives during WWII and changing modern medicine

questions.solution:
Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928. He observed that one of his Staphylococcus bacterial culture plates had been accidentally contaminated by a greenish mould (later identified as Penicillium notatum). Around the mould, there was a clear zone where bacterial colonies had been killed or prevented from growing. Fleming correctly concluded that the mould was producing some substance toxic to bacteria, which he named penicillin.

The discovery is considered accidental because Fleming had not planned any experiment involving mould. He had left a culture plate uncovered while going on holiday, and the contamination by airborne fungal spores occurred by chance. His insight lay in recognising the significance of this accidental observation rather than discarding the contaminated plate.

This discovery proved to be a milestone in medicine because penicillin became the world's first antibiotic used clinically to treat bacterial infections such as pneumonia, syphilis, and sepsis. During World War II, penicillin saved thousands of soldiers' lives. It opened the era of antibiotic therapy, fundamentally changing how infectious diseases are treated and reducing mortality from bacterial infections worldwide.

questions.text_english:
(a) What is the carrying capacity of a species in a habitat?
(b) Explain the growth curve that takes this capacity into account.

key_points: Carrying capacity (K): maximum population size that a habitat can support indefinitely given available resources
Logistic growth (S-shaped / sigmoid curve): dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K — population grows slowly at first, accelerates, then decelerates as it approaches K, forming an S-curve

questions.solution:
The carrying capacity (K) of a species in a habitat is the maximum number of individuals of that species that the habitat can sustain indefinitely without degradation of resources. It represents the upper limit of population size determined by the availability of food, space, water, and other environmental resources.

The growth curve that takes carrying capacity into account is the logistic growth curve, also called the sigmoid or S-shaped curve. It is described by the equation: dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, where N is population size, r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase, and K is the carrying capacity. In this model, when population size is small, growth is slow (lag phase), then it accelerates (log phase), and as N approaches K, growth slows again and eventually stops when N = K. This gives the characteristic S-shape. The factor (K-N)/K is called environmental resistance, which limits population growth as resources become scarce. This is the most realistic model of population growth in nature.

While ex situ conservation allows focused care and breeding of critically endangered species, it lacks the natural ecological interactions of the wild. (a) The following questions are based on the classic experiment conducted by Hershey and Chase.
(i) Why were bacteriophages chosen by the scientists?
(ii) Name the radioactive isotopes used and state the reason for using them.
(iii) Describe the steps of the experiment.
(iv) Why is this experiment considered a major breakthrough in the field of molecular biology?

key_points: Bacteriophages chosen because they have only two components — protein coat and DNA — making it easier to determine which one enters bacteria
Isotopes: 35S (radioactive sulphur) to label protein coat; 32P (radioactive phosphorus) to label DNA

Steps: Two batches of phages grown — one with 35S-labelled proteins, another with 32P-labelled DNA; phages allowed to infect E. coli; mixture blended to separate phage coats from bacteria; centrifuged; radioactivity detected in pellet (bacteria) vs supernatant
Breakthrough: conclusively proved that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material

questions.solution:
The Hershey-Chase experiment (1952) was designed to determine whether DNA or protein is the genetic material.

(i) Bacteriophages (T2 phage) were chosen because they consist of only two components — a protein coat and a DNA core — making them an ideal system to distinguish between the two candidate genetic materials.

(ii) Two radioactive isotopes were used. 35S (radioactive sulphur) was used to label phage proteins, because sulphur is present in amino acids (cysteine and methionine) but not in DNA. 32P (radioactive phosphorus) was used to label phage DNA, because phosphorus is present in the phosphate backbone of DNA but not in proteins.

(iii) Two batches of bacteriophages were prepared — one batch with 35S-labelled proteins, another with 32P-labelled DNA. Each batch was separately allowed to infect E. coli bacteria. After a short time, the mixture was placed in a blender to shear off phage coats from the bacterial surface. The mixture was then centrifuged — bacteria settled in the pellet while phage coats remained in the supernatant. Radioactivity was measured in both fractions. In the 35S experiment, radioactivity was found in the supernatant (phage protein coats), not the bacteria. In the 32P experiment, radioactivity was found inside the bacteria (pellet), confirming that DNA had entered the bacteria.

(iv) This experiment was a major breakthrough because it conclusively proved that DNA, not protein, is the genetic material that is injected by the phage into the host bacterium and carries heritable information. It resolved the longstanding debate about the nature of the genetic material and laid the foundation for all subsequent research in molecular biology and genetics.

questions.text_english:
(b) (i) What are multiple alleles? How do they differ from simple dominant-recessive allele pairs?
(ii) Explain the concept of multiple alleles with the help of a human trait studied by you.
(iii) Mention all possible genotypes with their corresponding phenotypes of the human trait as explained by you.
(iv) Comment on the type of inheritance pattern involved in the example explained by you.
questions.instruction_line_english: This is the alternative to question 31(a).

key_points: Multiple alleles: more than two alleles for a single gene locus in a population; in simple dominant-recessive only two alleles exist
Example: ABO blood groups — gene I with alleles IA, IB, and i
Genotypes and phenotypes: IAIA/IAi = Blood group A; IBIB/IBi = Blood group B; IAIB = Blood group AB; ii = Blood group O
Inheritance pattern: codominance (IA and IB both express in AB) and simple dominance (IA and IB over i)

questions.solution:
(i) Multiple alleles are defined as the existence of more than two allelic forms of a single gene at the same locus in a population, though any one individual can carry only two alleles (one on each homologous chromosome). In a simple dominant-recessive allele pair, only two alleles exist for a gene (e.g., A and a), and one is completely dominant over the other. In multiple allelism, three or more alleles exist in the population, and the relationships between them may be complex — involving dominance, recessiveness, or codominance in different combinations.

(ii) The classic example of multiple alleles in humans is the ABO blood group system. The gene governing ABO blood groups is the 'I' gene (for isoagglutinogen). It has three alleles: IA (codes for antigen A on RBCs), IB (codes for antigen B on RBCs), and i (codes for no antigen). IA and IB are both dominant over i, but codominant with each other.

(iii) All possible genotypes and their phenotypes are:
- IAIA → Blood group A
- IAi → Blood group A
- IBIB → Blood group B
- IBi → Blood group B
- IAIB → Blood group AB
- ii → Blood group O

(iv) The ABO blood group system involves two types of inheritance patterns. First, simple dominance: IA is dominant over i (IAIA and IAi both give blood group A), and IB is dominant over i (IBIB and IBi both give blood group B). Second, codominance: when both IA and IB alleles are present together (IAIB), both antigens A and B are expressed simultaneously on the RBC surface, producing blood group AB. Neither allele suppresses the other — this is called codominance. Thus, the ABO blood group is governed by both dominance and codominance.
questions.topic: Multiple alleles and ABO blood groups

questions.text_english:
(a) Oogenesis is a discontinuous process that begins before birth and is completed after puberty.
(i) Trace the development of a gamete mother cell till its release from the ovary during ovulation.
(ii) Name the two pituitary hormones that play an important role in the process.

key_points: Oogonium (2n) → Primary oocyte (mitosis, then arrested in Prophase I) → at puberty, Primary oocyte completes Meiosis I → Secondary oocyte + First polar body → Secondary oocyte arrested in Metaphase II → at fertilisation completes Meiosis II → Ovum + Second polar body
Two pituitary hormones: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) and LH (Luteinising Hormone)

questions.solution:
(i) Oogenesis begins during foetal development. Oogonia (diploid, 2n) in the ovary multiply by mitosis and then begin the first meiotic division, but arrest at the diplotene stage of Prophase I — these arrested cells are called primary oocytes. They remain in this arrested state, surrounded by granulosa cells forming a primary follicle, until puberty.

At puberty, under hormonal influence, a few primary follicles mature each month. The primary oocyte completes Meiosis I, producing an unequal division: a large secondary oocyte and a small first polar body. The secondary oocyte immediately enters Meiosis II but again arrests, this time at Metaphase II. At this stage, the secondary oocyte (along with the first polar body) is released from the Graafian follicle into the fallopian tube — this is ovulation. If fertilisation occurs, the secondary oocyte completes Meiosis II, producing the mature ovum and a second polar body. If fertilisation does not occur, the secondary oocyte degenerates without completing Meiosis II.

(ii) The two pituitary hormones involved are Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), which promotes the development and maturation of the follicle, and Luteinising Hormone (LH), whose surge at mid-cycle triggers ovulation and the release of the secondary oocyte from the Graafian follicle.

questions.text_english:
(b) (i) Draw a labelled two-celled structure of male gametophyte of an angiosperm.
(ii) Name the three layers that surround the cytoplasm of a male gametophyte starting from innermost to outermost layer.
(iii) Which organic material makes the outermost layer? Mention its advantage.
(iv) Why is the outermost layer of male gametophyte not continuous?
questions.instruction_line_english: This is the alternative to question 32(a).

key_points: Two-celled male gametophyte (pollen grain): one generative cell and one vegetative (tube) cell, with intine (inner wall) and exine (outer wall)
Three layers from innermost: plasma membrane, intine (cellulose and pectin), exine (sporopollenin)
Outermost layer (exine) made of sporopollenin — highly resistant to heat, acids, alkalis; protects pollen from harsh environments
Exine is not continuous because it has apertures (germ pores) through which the pollen tube germinates during pollination

questions.solution:
(i) A neat labelled diagram of a two-celled pollen grain (male gametophyte) should show: the large vegetative (tube) cell containing the vegetative nucleus, the smaller generative cell (with generative nucleus) lying within the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell, the inner intine wall, and the outer exine wall with apertures (germ pores).

(ii) The three layers surrounding the cytoplasm of the male gametophyte from innermost to outermost are: (1) Plasma membrane (plasmalemma) — the innermost living membrane. (2) Intine — the inner wall, composed of cellulose and pectin. (3) Exine — the tough outer wall, made of sporopollenin.

(iii) The outermost layer (exine) is made of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic compounds known. Its advantage is that it makes pollen extremely resistant to high temperatures, strong acids, strong alkalis, and enzymatic degradation. This ensures that pollen grains survive long-distance dispersal, adverse environmental conditions, and can be preserved in fossil records for millions of years.

(iv) The exine of the male gametophyte is not continuous because it has special openings called germ pores (apertures). These germ pores are essential for pollen tube germination — when the pollen grain lands on the stigma, the pollen tube emerges through a germ pore and grows down the style to deliver the male gametes to the ovule for fertilisation.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Explain any two basic principles/core techniques on which biotechnology is based.
(ii) Describe any three key tools used in Recombinant DNA technology.

key_points: Two principles: (1) Genetic engineering — ability to alter chemistry of genetic material and introduce it into host organisms; (2) Bioprocess engineering — maintaining sterile conditions to grow desired microbe/cell for production of biotechnological products

Three tools: (1) Restriction endonucleases — molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific sequences; (2) Vectors — carriers (plasmids, phages) that carry foreign DNA into host cell; (3) Host organism — the cell in which recombinant DNA is introduced and replicated

questions.solution:
(i) Biotechnology is based on two core principles:

First, Genetic Engineering: This refers to the ability to manipulate the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), alter its sequence, and introduce it into another organism to change the phenotype of the host. It includes techniques like restriction enzyme digestion, ligation, cloning, and PCR that allow scientists to cut, paste, copy, and transfer specific genes.

Second, Bioprocess Engineering (maintaining sterile conditions): This involves the use of sterile (aseptic) environments and bioreactors to enable the growth and maintenance of genetically engineered organisms under controlled conditions for large-scale production of desired biological products such as insulin, antibiotics, or vaccines.

(ii) Three key tools used in Recombinant DNA technology are:

1. Restriction Endonucleases (Molecular Scissors): These are enzymes that recognise specific palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA and cut the double-stranded DNA at or near those sequences, producing fragments with sticky ends or blunt ends. For example, EcoRI cuts at the sequence GAATTC. They allow precise cutting of both vector and foreign DNA.

2. Vectors (Cloning Vehicles): Vectors are DNA molecules that can carry a foreign DNA insert into a host cell and allow its replication. Common vectors include bacterial plasmids (e.g., pBR322), bacteriophages, cosmids, and BACs. A good vector must have an origin of replication, a selectable marker, and restriction sites.

3. Host Organisms: The host (e.g., E. coli, yeast, plant cells, animal cells) is the living system into which the recombinant DNA is introduced. The host must be able to take up the recombinant vector and replicate it, as well as express the inserted gene to produce the desired protein product.
questions.topic: Principles of biotechnology and tools of rDNA technology

questions.text_english:
(b) 'Early and accurate diagnosis of diseases is vital in medical technology.'
(i) Name the conventional methods of diagnosis and their disadvantages.
(ii) Which three diagnostic techniques have been developed through Biotechnology? Explain how each one helps in detecting diseases.
questions.instruction_line_english: This is the alternative to question 33(a).

key_points: Conventional methods: serological tests (based on antigen-antibody reaction) and microscopy; disadvantage: not sensitive enough at early stages when pathogen load is low
Three biotech techniques: (1) ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay), (2) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction), (3) Recombinant DNA technology-based probes / Southern blotting

questions.solution:
(i) The conventional methods of diagnosis include serological/immunological tests based on antigen-antibody interactions (such as agglutination tests, precipitation tests) and direct microscopic examination of blood or tissue samples. Their limitations are: they lack sensitivity and specificity at very early stages of infection when the pathogen concentration in the body is too low to produce a detectable immune response or visible signs. This means diseases may be missed in the early, most treatable stages.

(ii) Three biotechnology-based diagnostic techniques are:

1. ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay): ELISA detects the presence of either a specific antigen (pathogen component) or antibody in a patient's blood. In indirect ELISA, the patient's serum is added to wells coated with antigen; if specific antibodies are present, they bind. An enzyme-linked secondary antibody is then added; it binds to the primary antibody. Addition of substrate produces a colour change, detected by spectrophotometry. It is highly sensitive and widely used for HIV diagnosis and hepatitis detection.

2. PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction): PCR amplifies specific sequences of DNA or RNA (via RT-PCR) from a pathogen even when present in very small amounts. The target DNA undergoes repeated cycles of denaturation, annealing of primers, and extension. Even a single copy of pathogen DNA can be amplified millions of times and detected. PCR is used to detect HIV in early infection, genetic disorders, and in forensic medicine.

3. DNA Probes (Southern Blotting / Hybridisation): Radioactively or fluorescently labelled single-stranded DNA sequences (probes) complementary to the pathogen's specific gene sequence are used. Patient's DNA/RNA is denatured and hybridised with the probe; if the target sequence is present, the probe binds and signal is detected. This technique identifies specific pathogens and can also detect mutations causing genetic diseases.
questions.topic: Diagnostic techniques in medicine — ELISA, PCR, DNA probes
